route: The realisation set Real_1(s) of a cube orientation by one-player readout systems, attacked not as a bilinear semialgebraic set to be relaxed, but through its FACET DATA. Freezing one Max vertex turns Real_1(s) into a fibred product: the facet's own realisation set, times the condition that the frozen vertex's action difference D_u = Psi_{u,1} - Psi_{u,0} — an affine functional of the remaining values — separate the facet's value configuration along the colouring b_u. The certificate of emptiness is then not a Farkas vector of a McCormick relaxation (that relaxation is feasible, and the level-one RLT-in-(psi,chi) relaxation is feasible too — both were tried and discarded) but a RADON CIRCUIT of the facet's value configuration whose five 4x4 determinant signs are forced by the facet orientation alone. The signs are read off two "line identities" that make each determinant an explicit signed combination of the switching gaps; the two derivations of the fifth determinant, along the two edge-paths from y_0 to y_3, are negative on complementary sides of the comparison delta_5 vs delta_6, so their disjunction settles it.
object: The facet datum of a cube orientation — an (m-1)-cube orientation t together with the 2-colouring chi = b_u of its vertices by the frozen coordinate's preferred action — and its CO-REALISABILITY: the demand that some one-player system realising t have its 2^{m-1} value vectors strictly split by an affine functional along chi; equivalently, a demand on the oriented matroid of that value configuration, which the paper's readout theory never asked of it.
headline: The Holt–Klee acyclic unique sink orientation s_0 = (8,9,10,11,13,12,14,15,7,6,4,5,3,2,1,0) of the 4-cube is not the improvement orientation of any nondegenerate one-player stopping SSG, so at m = 4 one-player realisability is strictly stronger than the Holt–Klee condition.

results.name: hkc:facet — the facet lemma
results.statement: Let s be the improvement outmap of a nondegenerate one-player stopping SSG with m Max vertices and b(sigma) := sigma xor s(sigma). For every coordinate u and every a in {0,1} the facet datum D_{u,a}(s) — the restriction of s to H = {sigma : sigma_u = a}, read as an outmap t of the (m-1)-cube on the coordinates other than u, together with the colouring chi := b_u|_H — is CO-REALISABLE: there is a nondegenerate one-player stopping SSG with m-1 Max vertices whose improvement outmap is t and whose value configuration (y_sigma) admits an affine functional phi on R^{m-1} with phi(y_sigma) > 0 exactly when chi(sigma) = 1. The same holds for every subcube in place of a facet and every frozen coordinate u.
results.why_not_implied: lem:crossing(c) is the 2-face case and only for the colouring that is the split by the face's OWN non-constant coordinate; it says nothing about the colouring b_u of a frozen coordinate on a face of dimension > 2, and its consequence cor:b2-min excludes no Holt–Klee class of the 4-cube while the 3-dimensional case proved here excludes thirteen.
results.argument: Freeze u at a (def:subcube). Substituting x_u = Psi_{u,a}(x_{-u}) into Psi_{v,c} for v != u and eliminating the self-entry p^{v,c}_u p^{u,a}_v < 1 (lem:readout-reduce) gives substochastic affine maps with zero self-entry (the row sums do not grow: sum_{w != u} p̃_w + q̃ <= |p^{v,c}|_1 + q^{v,c}); at the fixed point the substitution is an identity, so the reduced system's value vectors are x_sigma restricted to Vmax minus u for sigma in H, its improvement margins have the same signs as the original's, and by lem:subgame(a),(b) it is a stopping game with m-1 Max vertices whose outmap is s|_H. Finally D_u = Psi_{u,1} - Psi_{u,0} is affine with zero coefficient at x_u, so it IS an affine functional of the reduced values, and its sign at x_sigma is b_u(sigma) by nondegeneracy.
results.verification: Validated computationally on 40 exact 4-Max readout systems of the round-18 survey x 2 freezings (reduce_check.py): in 80 of 80 cases the reduced 3-state system's 8 value vectors equal x_sigma restricted to the free coordinates, its outmap equals the facet of the 4-cube outmap, and the facet colouring b_0 is separated (exact values, float LP for the separation only). Also verified FROM THE GAME on three explicit 4-Max one-player stopping SSGs built from those systems by lem:dyadic-row (138, 139, 157 vertices; m4_game_check.py, M4_game0.json): greatest trap empty, outmap from the game equal to the class outmap, least margins 1485575/67108864, 46424129723/344004991047680, 396464791181/29610042781952, and for all four coordinates and both actions D_u has zero coefficient at x_u and its sign at each of the 16 game-computed value vectors equals b_u.

results.name: hkc:obstruction — a facet datum that is not co-realisable
results.statement: Index {0,1}^3 by sigma = sigma_0 + 2 sigma_1 + 4 sigma_2. For t = (4,5,6,7,3,2,1,0) and the colouring chi with chi^{-1}(1) = {2,4,6,7}, chi^{-1}(0) = {0,1,3,5}, the pair (t,chi) is NOT co-realisable, although t is an acyclic Holt–Klee unique sink orientation of the 3-cube of bottom-antipodal height 2 realised by nondegenerate one-player stopping SSGs.
results.why_not_implied: cor:parity-unreadable is the single statement of this species in the paper — no affine functional of the value vector has the sign of the height parity of B^1 — and it is proved by lem:crossing on ONE 2-face where the colouring happens to be a face split; here the colouring is a face split on no 2-face at all, so lem:crossing is silent, and the certificate is a 5-point Radon circuit meeting both facets sigma_2 = 0 and sigma_2 = 1.
results.argument: From b(sigma) = sigma xor t(sigma) = 4 for sigma <= 3 and 7 for sigma >= 4: sign D_0(y_sigma) = sign D_1(y_sigma) = 2 sigma_2 - 1 and delta_sigma := D_2(y_sigma) > 0, all nonzero by nondegeneracy; and by lem:switch y_3 <= y_1 <= y_0, y_3 <= y_2 <= y_0, strict at the coordinate switched. Shear (y(0),y(1),y(2)) -> (u,h) with u = (y(0),y(1)) and h = y(2) - Psi_{2,0}(y): h_sigma = sigma_2 delta_sigma, so the 4x4 determinant D(i,j,k,l) of the homogeneous points becomes delta_k [u_i u_j u_l] - delta_l [u_i u_j u_k] for i,j low and k,l high, and -delta_l [u_i u_j u_k] when only l is high. Two line identities: with S_{a,c}(u) := p^{0,a}_1 u^2 + p^{0,a}_2 rho_c(u) + q^{0,a} and R_{b,c} its analogue at state 1, V^{a,c}(sigma) = u^1_sigma - S_{a,c}(u_sigma) = (sigma_0 - a) D_0(y_sigma) + p^{0,a}_2 (sigma_2 - c) delta_sigma and W^{b,c}(sigma) = (sigma_1 - b) D_1(y_sigma) + p^{1,b}_2 (sigma_2 - c) delta_sigma; the gradients of u^1 - S and u^2 - R have a positive first (resp. second) component because a product p^{0,a}_2 p^{2,c}_0 = 1 would close a sink-free 2-cycle against stopping, so for i,j on a common line [u_i u_j w] = -(u^2_j - u^2_i) lambda (w^1 - S(w)) resp. (u^1_j - u^1_i) mu (w^2 - R(w)). Evaluating at sigma = 3,5,6 the products p_2 delta_5 delta_6 CANCEL and D(0,2,5,6) = -B delta_6 D_0(y_5) < 0, D(2,3,5,6) = -A delta_6 D_1(y_5) < 0, D(0,2,3,k) = -delta_k B D_0(y_3) > 0 for k = 5,6, with A,B > 0 the four positive scalars built from the strict order relations. For the fifth, the plane identity [u_0 u_3 w] = [u_2 u_3 w] + [u_0 u_2 w] - [u_0 u_2 u_3] gives D(0,3,5,6) = -A delta_6 D_1(y_5) - B delta_6 D_0(y_5) + B |D_0(y_3)| (delta_5 - delta_6), and its companion along the other path y_0 -> y_1 -> y_3 gives D(0,3,5,6) = -B' delta_5 D_0(y_6) - A' delta_5 D_1(y_6) - K (delta_5 - delta_6) with K = [u_0 u_1 u_3] > 0; the first is negative when delta_5 <= delta_6, the second when delta_5 >= delta_6, so D(0,3,5,6) < 0 in every case. Laplace expansion on the support S = (0,2,3,5,6) then gives mu with sum mu_i Y_i = 0, sum mu_i = 0 and mu_0 = D(2,3,5,6) < 0, mu_2 = -D(0,3,5,6) > 0, mu_3 = D(0,2,5,6) < 0, mu_5 = -D(0,2,3,6) < 0, mu_6 = D(0,2,3,5) > 0 — positive exactly on {2,6} subset of chi^{-1}(1) and negative exactly on {0,3,5} subset of chi^{-1}(0). Any affine phi with the signs of chi would make every mu_i phi(y_i) strictly positive while their sum is 0.
results.verification: All exact (fractions.Fraction). 43 DISTINCT exact dyadic readout systems realising t were produced (3 at denominator 2^10, 40 at 2^18/2^20/2^24) and every identity of the proof recomputed on each of them: the line identities (hkc:eq-VL, hkc:eq-VM) as equalities for all 8 sigma and all (a,c), the positivity of s_L, s_M, s'_L, s'_M and of A,A',B',B and K, the four closed formulas for D(0,2,5,6), D(2,3,5,6), D(0,2,3,5), D(0,2,3,6), BOTH expressions E1 and E2 for D(0,3,5,6) as exact equalities, and the Radon identity sum mu_i Y_i = 0 with the signs of chi — 43/43 on every item, 7 of the 43 with delta_5 > delta_6 so that the E2 branch is exercised. The two line identities were in addition verified SYMBOLICALLY (sympy) in the 18 free row parameters, for all 8 strategies and all four (a,c). Independently, over 1500 float systems realising t the 70 quadruple determinants take only 8 distinct sign vectors, the 6 zeros are exactly the 6 coplanar 2-faces, and the five determinants of the circuit are constant in sign; the separation LP returns margin exactly 0 on every one of 2247 sampled systems. Direct search evidence: the improved optimiser drives the min margin of a 4-Max system for s_0 to -2.4e-5 over 72 restarts and no further, with the whole violation at coordinate 0 and vertex 0's two rows collapsing together.

results.name: hkc:main — Holt–Klee is not sufficient at m = 4
results.statement: s_0 = (8,9,10,11,13,12,14,15,7,6,4,5,3,2,1,0) is an acyclic Holt–Klee unique sink orientation of the 4-cube of bottom-antipodal height 2 and is not the improvement orientation of any nondegenerate one-player stopping SSG. Exactly 17 of the 12640 classes of acyclic unique sink orientations of the 4-cube carry a facet datum isomorphic to (t,chi) and are therefore not one-player realisable; 13 of them are Holt–Klee, of heights 2, 3, 4 with multiplicities 3, 6, 4. Hence prop:m3-realised does not extend: at m = 4 one-player realisability is strictly stronger than the Holt–Klee condition.
results.why_not_implied: rem:hk-survey records a failed search over 162 classes, says explicitly 'a failed search is not a result', and draws the OPPOSITE reading ('at m = 4, then, Holt–Klee appears to be the whole condition for one-player realisability; this is a measurement'); it contains no non-realisability proof for any Holt–Klee class, and the class named there as the smallest candidate is exactly s_0.
results.argument: s_0's preferred-action vector is (8,8,8,8,9,9,8,8,15,15,14,14,15,15,15,15), so b_1 = b_2 = sigma_3 and b_3 = 1 — the facet sigma_0 = 0 read on the coordinates 1,2,3 is exactly t — while b_0 takes the value 1 at sigma in {4,5,8,9,12,13,14,15}, i.e. chi^{-1}(1) = {2,4,6,7} in the facet's own indexing. Apply hkc:facet and hkc:obstruction. The count of 17 is the enumeration of the 8 facet data of each of the 12640 class representatives against the 96-element isomorphism orbit of (t,chi) under the 48 automorphisms of the 3-cube and colour complementation.
results.verification: s_0 checked here to be a USO, acyclic, of BA height 2 with sink 15 and walk 0,8,15, and Holt–Klee by a unit vertex-capacity max-flow on every face of every dimension (my_D.py, validated on the 12 AUSOs of the 2-cube and on G#). The exclusion scan over all 12640 class representatives gives 17 classes, 13 Holt–Klee (heights 2,3,4 with multiplicities 3,6,4) and 4 not; every one of the 17 was re-confirmed by explicitly exhibiting the facet (u,a) and the 3-cube automorphism carrying its datum to (t,chi) (excluded_17.json). Cross-checks: all 13 excluded Holt–Klee classes lie among the 162 the round-18 survey left unresolved, and NONE of the 5951 classes that survey realised is excluded — a check that would have refuted either the law or one of those realisations. cor:b2-min's forbidden-pair test, re-implemented here from its statement, reproduces its published counts (0 of 6113 Holt–Klee classes, 4365 of the 6527 others) and does not fire on s_0, so the new law is not that test. Search consistency: on each of the 13 the improved optimiser attains a best min-margin between -7.3e-5 and -1.1e-4 and no better.

restatements.label: lem:crossing
restatements.note: Steps 1–2 of my proof re-derive its content in the one-player case: the four value vectors of a 2-face lie in an affine plane, in it the two sigma_i-segments meet iff g_i is non-constant on the face, and then no affine functional separates them. I found this only after re-deriving it as the 'flat lines meet steep lines' picture; my first candidate law ('b_u is never diagonal on a 2-face') was FALSE and was killed by exactly this lemma's geometry — 48 Holt–Klee AUSOs of the 3-cube violate it and are realised.

restatements.label: cor:b2-min
restatements.note: The forbidden-pair test as a local necessary condition for one-player realisability; I re-implemented it from its statement and reproduced its counts exactly (0 of the 6113 Holt–Klee classes of the 4-cube, 4365 of the 6527 others). A forbidden pair (F,c) with c outside F is precisely the 2-dimensional case of my facet datum.

restatements.label: cor:parity-unreadable
restatements.note: The species 'no affine functional of the value vector has the sign of a prescribed colouring' is already in the paper (there for the height parity of B^1, and in prop:parity-readable(a) for B^2's realisation); what is new here is that b_u on a facet is such a colouring and that this is a necessary condition for realisability one dimension up.

restatements.label: prop:oneplayer-lp
restatements.note: That the improvement orientation of a nondegenerate one-player game is induced by the scalar f(sigma) = sum_v val_sigma(v) on the cube — I re-derived this from the objective clause before finding it stated; it is exactly the edge clause of prop:oneplayer-lp.

gap: MISSING STATEMENT: whether co-realisability of every facet datum, together with Holt–Klee, characterises one-player realisability at m = 4 — equivalently, whether each of the remaining 149 Holt–Klee classes of the 4-cube left unresolved by the round-18 survey and not excluded by hkc:obstruction is the improvement orientation of a nondegenerate one-player stopping SSG. My exploratory sweep of all 2024 canonical facet data occurring in the 12640 classes (scan2.py) tested separability against 100 sampled systems per facet orientation and would exclude 132 Holt–Klee classes, 130 of them among the 162; but two of its exclusions (classes 411 and 425, height 5) are classes round 18 realised, so at that sample size the test is UNSOUND and its numbers are not evidence — only the one datum proved here stands.
next_steps: 1. Prove more data non-co-realisable by the same machinery. The proof needed only: the sign pattern of the three D_v on the 8 strategies, four strict order relations, and the two line identities. Everything after that is mechanical — enumerate the 4- and 5-point circuits of the 8 homogeneous value points, express each 4x4 determinant through the line identities as a signed combination of gaps, and look for a circuit all of whose determinant signs are forced. This can be automated over all 2024 canonical facet data; the sweep says 130 of the 162 are candidates. 2. Replace the sampled separability oracle by an exact one: for a FIXED 3-cube orientation the separable dichotomies of its value configurations are governed by the 8 chirotopes observed, which are themselves determined by a small number of forced determinant signs; computing that chirotope set exactly would decide co-realisability for all 256 colourings at once and settle the 149. 3. Push to m = 5: by hkc:remark(f) the obstruction fires on any 3-dimensional subcube with a frozen coordinate, so the 13 excluded 4-cube classes propagate; check whether any facet of prop:hstar-one-eleven's height-11 witness or of the Holt–Klee height-11 class of prop:hkfive that is NOT realised carries an obstructed datum, which would give the first entry of the four-ceiling table where h*_1^{nd} < h*_HK. 4. Two players: thm:min-count says a non-Holt–Klee orientation needs Min vertices in proportion to the Holt–Klee defect; the analogous question here is how many Min vertices an obstructed datum costs — for r pieces the readout Psi_{u,a} is a MINIMUM of affine maps, so D_u is a difference of two concave functions and the separation becomes a difference-of-concave sign pattern rather than an affine one. A lower bound k >= 1 for the 13 classes should follow at once; whether k = 1 suffices is open.

prior_art: From memory, flagged unchecked against the sources. (i) The certificate is Radon's theorem / the circuit signs of an oriented matroid; that a set of points admits no separating hyperplane for a prescribed dichotomy iff a circuit's sign vector is compatible with it is standard oriented-matroid theory (Bland–Las Vergnas, Björner–Las Vergnas–Sturmfels–White). Nothing beyond linear algebra is imported: the certificate is exhibited, not invoked. (ii) The occupancy polytope of a transient two-action MDP is, in the reduced form used here, a Leontief substitution system {y >= 0 : By = 1} with exactly one positive entry per column (Koehler–Whinston–Wright, Veinott); the paper already has the polytope (prop:oneplayer-lp, d'Epenoux) but not the Leontief reading, which I did not need. (iii) The statement that realisable USOs are Holt–Klee is Gärtner–Morris–Ruest, already imported by the paper; my theorem says its converse fails at m = 4, which I have not seen anywhere and which the USO literature (Schurr–Szabó, Gärtner) appears to leave open in the form 'which USOs are LP orientations of occupancy polytopes'. (iv) The four-points-in-a-plane structure of a 2-face is lem:crossing in the paper and, in the LP reading, the fact that a 2-face of a simple polytope with a linear objective has its two edge-pairs' segments crossing exactly when the objective is non-monotone across it.
